newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman ready for talks with Israel on peace process.
newsitem.headline: Oman ready for talks with Israel on peace process.

text.p: Oman said on Monday it was ready to talk to Israel to push the Middle East peace process after the Jewish state signed a deal on Palestinian self-rule in the West Bank town of Hebron, the official news agency ONA said.
Oman last month froze commercial ties with Israel and said this would not be relaxed until the Jewish state adhered to previous commitments to the Palestinian leadership.

"We hope the deal is a new turn that would guarantee the Palestinian brethren the strength and power to continue their talks with the Israeli side," ONA quoted Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Youssef bin Alawi bin Abdullah as saying.
"His excellency also noted the sultanate's readiness to talk to Israel in order to support the peace process in the Middle East on all tracks after the Hebron obstacle was removed," ONA added.

Last week Israel and the Palestinians reached agreement to transfer control of 80 percent of Hebron to self-rule. Israeli soldiers left their headquarters on Friday and on Sunday Palestinian President Yasser Arafat visited the city.
Bin Alawi said Arabs should continue efforts to convince Israel of the importance of peace with Lebanon and Syria on the basis agreed to at the 1991 Middle East peace conference.
